messages.subject: measurementInvarianceCat error/bug?
parts:
Hi, I’m trying to run measurementInvarianceCat function on my dichotomous data. Unfortunately I got stuck getting this error message again and again:


Error in measurementInvarianceCat(model = L.mod1, data = NoSlovak, group = "soubor",  :

  object 'fitScalar' not found

 

Definition of the model:

L.mod1 <- "

L =~

i16+  i29+  i41+  i51+  i44+  i93+  i102+ i107+ i123+ i139+ i153+ i183+ i203+ i232+ i260

"

measurementInvarianceCat command:

L.fittest <- measurementInvarianceCat(model = L.mod1, data = NoSlovak,

              group = "soubor", parametrization="theta", estimator="wlsmv",

      ordered = c("i16", "i29", "i41", "i51", "i44", "i93", "i102", "i107", "i123", "i139", "i153", "i183", "i203" ,"i232" ,"i260"))

 

Does anyone have experience with this issue too please? If any additional information needed, please let me know. I’ll be really grateful for any advice.


(At first I tried to test the invariance by running models with  loadings/thresholds/residuals fixed to be equal across groups, but as I wasn’t able to fix the residuals (the fit indexes for models with non/fixed residuals didn’t differ), the measurementInvarianceCat function seemed like the only option.)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvarianceCat error/bug?
parts:
getting this error message again and again:


Error in measurementInvarianceCat(model = L.mod1, data = NoSlovak, group = "soubor",  :

  object 'fitScalar' not found

This means the scalar model did not converge.  This looks like something that got fixed a while ago.  Does it still happen in the latest development version?

install.packages("lavaan", repos="http://www.da.ugent.be", type="source")
devtools::install_github("simsem/semTools/semTools")

(At first I tried to test the invariance by running models with  loadings/thresholds/residuals fixed to be equal across groups, but as I wasn’t able to fix the residuals (the fit indexes for models with non/fixed residuals didn’t differ), the measurementInvarianceCat function seemed like the only option.)

I would never recommend automation as an alternative finding out what the problem was with your own script.  Can you post that?  If you did not set parameterization = "theta", then under the default parameterization = "delta" you are unable to fix or constrain any residual variances.   The scripts Christopher posted will show you the models that measurementInvarianceCat() fits automatically, but I plan to rewrite that function this year, in light of new research.  

FYI, you cannot separately identify any measurement parameters with binary data, so make sure you only compare a configural model to a model in which both loadings and thresholds are constrained across groups (and intercepts are fixed to zero, which lavaan does by default) to test scalar invariance.  Then, to test strict invariance, you fix all residual variances to 1 (they have to be fixed to 1 in one group for identification, so testing equality across groups requires fixing all groups' residual variances to 1).
